prompt: The choice a barangay resident marks for a local candidate is a ___.
fact: In the BSKE, voters choose the Punong Barangay, seven Barangay Kagawad, and the SK officials they are eligible to vote for.

prompt: A registered barangay resident who can cast a ballot is a ___.
fact: Regular barangay voters must be Filipino citizens who are at least 18 on election day and meet the residence requirements.

prompt: The paper used to choose barangay and SK officials is the ___.
fact: A voter marks the ballot carefully so each chosen barangay or SK candidate can be counted.

prompt: The agency that conducts barangay and SK elections is ___.
fact: COMELEC manages voter registration, polling rules, and the official BSKE calendar.

prompt: The smallest local government unit in the Philippines is the ___.
fact: The barangay is the level of government closest to daily life, and every Filipino lives in one.

prompt: A member of the barangay council is a barangay ___.
fact: A Sangguniang Barangay has seven elected Kagawad, who pass the barangay's local ordinances.

prompt: After voting in the BSKE, indelible ___ is placed on a voter's finger.
fact: Indelible ink helps election workers prevent anyone from voting twice.

prompt: The minimum age to run for an elected SK position is ___.
fact: An elected SK candidate must be 18 to 24 years old on election day.

prompt: The voting area assigned to a barangay resident is their ___.
fact: COMELEC assigns a voter's precinct using the address in their registration record.

prompt: A barangay voter's choice must remain ___.
fact: The secret ballot protects every BSKE voter from pressure or intimidation.

prompt: After the BSKE polls close, the electoral board ___ the votes.
fact: Counting happens at the precinct where accredited watchers may observe the process.

prompt: Barangay residents go to the ___ to cast their ballots.
fact: BSKE polling places are commonly located in public schools.

prompt: The highest age allowed for an elected SK candidate is ___.
fact: An elected SK candidate must not be older than 24 on election day.

prompt: The youth assembly in every barangay is the Katipunan ng ___.
fact: The Katipunan ng Kabataan includes registered barangay residents who are 15 to 30 years old.

prompt: An SK candidate must have lived in the barangay for at least one ___.
fact: The one-year barangay residence requirement is measured immediately before election day.

prompt: The Punong Barangay is commonly called the barangay ___.
fact: Punong Barangay is the official title of the elected head of the barangay.

prompt: The Filipino word for a choice cast in a barangay election is ___.
fact: The reminder 'ang boto mo ay mahalaga' emphasizes that every barangay vote matters.

prompt: Barangay residents vote to choose a local ___.
fact: In a barangay election you choose a Punong Barangay and seven Kagawad on the same ballot.

prompt: A Sangguniang Barangay has ___ elected Barangay Kagawad.
fact: The Punong Barangay leads the council, while seven Barangay Kagawad help pass local ordinances.

prompt: SK voters aged 15 to 17 vote for SK positions ___.
fact: Voters aged 15 to 17 participate only in the SK part of the BSKE.

prompt: Voters aged 18 to 30 may vote in ___ regular barangay and SK elections.
fact: Eligible voters aged 18 to 30 may vote for both regular barangay and SK positions.

prompt: Voters aged 31 and above vote for ___ barangay positions.
fact: Voters aged 31 and above no longer vote in the SK election but may vote for regular barangay positions.

prompt: The SK receives ten ___ of the barangay general fund.
fact: Ten percent of the barangay general fund is set aside for youth development and empowerment through the SK.

prompt: The barangay justice system is called Katarungang ___.
fact: Katarungang Pambarangay helps settle certain community disputes at the barangay level.

prompt: Barangay office is a public ___.
fact: Officials must act with integrity and remain accountable to the people at all times.

prompt: The SK gives the barangay's ___ a voice in local government.
fact: The SK represents young residents and develops programs for their needs.

prompt: The SK chairperson also sits on the barangay ___.
fact: The SK chairperson serves as an ex officio member of the Sangguniang Barangay.

prompt: Money reserved for SK youth programs is the SK ___.
fact: The SK fund supports programs such as education, sports, the environment, health, and livelihood.

prompt: Residents discuss community issues at the barangay ___.
fact: The barangay assembly meets at least twice a year to discuss local activities, finances, and community concerns.

prompt: A person running for barangay or SK office is a ___.
fact: Someone becomes an official candidate only after filing a Certificate of Candidacy with COMELEC.

prompt: A barangay or SK candidate files a ___ to run for office.
fact: The Certificate of Candidacy names the office sought and declares that the filer is eligible for it.

prompt: A barangay candidate should explain their ___ for the community.
fact: Always ask how a plan will be paid for: a barangay's funds come largely from its share of national taxes.

prompt: A public gathering for a barangay campaign is a ___.
fact: Campaigning outside the official campaign period set by COMELEC is prohibited.

prompt: Candidates answer questions side by side in a ___.
fact: A barangay debate lets voters compare plans directly instead of judging by posters alone.

prompt: Printed BSKE campaign material displayed in public is a ___.
fact: COMELEC limits poster size and allows them only in designated common poster areas.

prompt: A barangay candidate's past performance is their track ___.
fact: Attendance at council sessions and finished projects are checkable evidence, unlike promises.

prompt: A realistic plan must fit the barangay's ___.
fact: A barangay must set aside part of its budget for the SK and for disaster risk reduction.

prompt: The length of time an official serves is their ___.
fact: Republic Act 12232 set a four-year term for barangay and SK officials and moved the elections to the first Monday of November 2026.

prompt: A winning barangay official takes an ___ of office before serving.
fact: The oath binds the official to defend the Constitution and discharge their duties faithfully.

prompt: Barangay and SK candidates run without a political ___.
fact: Barangay and SK elections are non-partisan, so candidates there run without party backing.

prompt: Voters should look for an ___ barangay candidate.
fact: Officials file a yearly statement of assets, liabilities and net worth that the public may inspect.

prompt: Paying a barangay resident for their vote is vote ___.
fact: Vote buying is an election offense, and the law can hold both the giver and the receiver liable.

prompt: Using a ___ to control someone's BSKE vote is illegal.
fact: Intimidating a voter is an election offense; report it to COMELEC or to a poll watcher.

prompt: A ___ social media post about a barangay candidate can mislead voters.
fact: Check a surprising election claim against COMELEC's official channels before sharing it.

prompt: An unverified story about a barangay candidate is a ___.
fact: A claim repeated many times does not become true; trace it back to its original source.

prompt: An accusation against a barangay candidate needs ___.
fact: Ask who published a claim, when they published it, and what evidence they actually showed.

prompt: Carrying firearms is barred during the election period under the ___.
fact: COMELEC imposes a nationwide gun ban for the whole election period to keep the polls peaceful.

prompt: A person who monitors the polls for a group is a poll ___.
fact: Accredited watchers may observe the counting and receive their own copy of the results.

prompt: A voter who witnesses cheating in the BSKE should ___ it.
fact: COMELEC runs reporting hotlines and an anti-vote-buying campaign for exactly this purpose.

prompt: Before believing a claim about a barangay candidate, check its ___.
fact: An official result comes from COMELEC, not from a social media post or a group chat forward.

prompt: The elected head of a barangay is the ___.
fact: The Punong Barangay presides over the Sangguniang Barangay but may only vote to break a tie.

prompt: The local legislative council of an LGU is called the ___.
fact: The barangay's version, the Sangguniang Barangay, passes ordinances binding within the barangay.

prompt: The right of citizens to vote is called ___.
fact: Article V of the Constitution bars any literacy, property or other substantive test on suffrage.

prompt: Living in an area long enough to vote there is the ___ requirement.
fact: A voter must have lived in the Philippines for one year and in their locality for six months.

prompt: A voter who moves to a new city files a ___ of registration.
fact: Without transferring, your name stays in your old precinct and you must return there to vote.

prompt: The fingerprint and photo taken at registration are a voter's ___.
fact: Biometrics let COMELEC detect one person registering twice under different names.

prompt: Adding up precinct results to get a total is called ___.
fact: Canvassing happens in public before a board of canvassers, with watchers entitled to observe.

prompt: The board of canvassers will ___ the winners.
fact: Only proclamation makes a win official; leading an unofficial tally is not the same as winning.

prompt: A voter who deliberately leaves a race blank chooses to ___.
fact: An abstention is not an invalid ballot: the rest of your choices are still counted.

prompt: Marking more names than allowed in a race is an ___.
fact: Only the over-voted race is voided; your other choices on the same ballot still count.

prompt: The share of registered voters who actually vote is the ___.
fact: Philippine turnout is high by world standards, often well above two thirds of registered voters.

prompt: All the people entitled to vote form the ___.
fact: The electorate grows every election as newly registered 18-year-olds join the rolls.

prompt: A direct vote to approve a proposed change to law is a ___.
fact: Creating, merging or abolishing a barangay requires a plebiscite among the affected voters.

prompt: The seat of barangay government is the ___.
fact: The barangay hall is where the council meets and where residents file blotter reports and clearances.

prompt: A local law passed by a Sanggunian is an ___.
fact: A barangay ordinance binds only within that barangay and cannot override national law.

prompt: Government where citizens choose their leaders is a ___.
fact: The Constitution calls the Philippines a democratic and republican state where sovereignty resides in the people.

prompt: The protection that keeps a vote unknown is ballot ___.
fact: Secrecy is a safeguard, not a courtesy: it is what makes buying or coercing a vote unenforceable.

prompt: Officials must be ___ to the people who elected them.
fact: Article XI makes public officials accountable and provides for their removal from office.

prompt: Open and inspectable government processes are ___.
fact: Barangay budgets must be posted publicly so residents can see how funds are spent.

prompt: Freedom from corruption or improper influence is ___.
fact: Officials swear to serve with integrity and file yearly declarations of their wealth.

prompt: The meeting where barangay residents are consulted is the barangay ___.
fact: The barangay assembly must be held at least twice a year and any resident may attend.

prompt: A state where power is exercised through elected representatives is a ___.
fact: The Philippines is a democratic and republican state under Article II of the Constitution.

prompt: In the Philippines the people are ___.
fact: Sovereignty resides in the people, and all government authority comes from them.

prompt: A voter who decides using reliable information is an ___ voter.
fact: Comparing a candidate's record against their promises is the core habit of informed voting.

prompt: Teaching citizens their electoral rights is voter ___.
fact: COMELEC and schools run voter education drives before every election.

prompt: Making sure every group can take part is ___.
fact: Persons with disabilities, seniors and detainees have special voting arrangements so they are not excluded.

prompt: Polling places must be ___ to voters with disabilities.
fact: COMELEC provides ground-floor accessible polling places and allows an assistor for those who need one.

prompt: Citizens who take part in public life ___.
fact: Voting is one form of participation; attending the barangay assembly is another.

prompt: The authority voters give a winner is their ___.
fact: A mandate is limited by law: an official may only exercise the powers the office actually has.

prompt: Article XI says public office is a ___.
fact: Officials must serve with responsibility, integrity, loyalty and efficiency, and act with patriotism and justice.

prompt: Election officials must remain ___.
fact: The electoral board must treat every candidate the same, whatever their own preference.

prompt: Duties a citizen owes the community are ___ duties.
fact: Registering, voting and reporting offenses are all civic duties in an election.

prompt: A voter's freedom to choose without control is voter ___.
fact: Voting inside a private booth is the practical guarantee of that freedom.

prompt: A candidate's stated programme of action is their ___.
fact: Ask whether a platform names a funding source; a barangay cannot spend money it does not have.

prompt: The period of public persuasion before voting is the ___.
fact: COMELEC sets fixed campaign period dates, and campaigning outside them is an offense.

prompt: Filing a certificate of ___ makes someone an official candidate.
fact: A filer who is not actually eligible for the office can have their certificate cancelled.

prompt: COMELEC may reject a ___ candidate.
fact: A nuisance candidate is one filing to mock the process or to confuse voters with a similar name.

prompt: A candidate must be legally ___ for the office.
fact: A barangay candidate must be a registered voter of that barangay and a resident for at least one year.

prompt: The official currently holding the post is the ___.
fact: An incumbent's record is checkable: look at finished projects and session attendance.

prompt: A candidate meeting every legal requirement is ___.
fact: Age, citizenship, residence and voter registration are the basic qualifications for barangay office.

prompt: A pledge made while campaigning is a campaign ___.
fact: Compare a promise against the office's real powers: a Punong Barangay cannot build a national highway.

prompt: A plan that can realistically be done is ___.
fact: Feasibility means asking about money, manpower and time, not just whether the idea sounds good.

prompt: A specific public works plan is a barangay ___.
fact: Barangay projects must appear in the barangay development plan before funds can be released.

prompt: Work done for the community is public ___.
fact: Public service is measured by what reaches residents, not by how visible the official is.

prompt: A candidate's previous relevant work is their ___.
fact: Experience is only useful evidence if you can verify it independently.

prompt: Padding one candidate's votes while shaving another's is ___.
fact: Dagdag-bawas alters the tally during canvassing, which is why public canvassing and watchers matter.

prompt: Someone who votes in a precinct where they do not belong is a ___.
fact: Biometric registration and indelible ink exist specifically to stop flying voters.

prompt: Forcing a person to vote a certain way is ___.
fact: Coercion is an election offense whether the pressure comes from an employer, a neighbour or a relative.

prompt: An act punished under election law is an election ___.
fact: Election offenses can carry imprisonment and disqualification from holding public office.

prompt: To spread false claims deliberately is to ___.
fact: Disinformation is deliberate; misinformation is the same falsehood shared by someone who believed it.

prompt: A citizen wrongly prevented from voting has been ___.
fact: Failing to vote in two consecutive regular elections can deactivate a registration, which is why reactivation drives exist.

prompt: Restoring a deactivated registration requires ___.
fact: A voter whose record was deactivated must file for reactivation with the local COMELEC office before the deadline.

prompt: The teachers who run a precinct on election day form the ___.
fact: The board verifies each voter's identity, issues the ballot and oversees the counting machine.

prompt: The document carrying totals up to the next canvassing level is the ___.
fact: Each certificate of canvass is signed and copies go to watchers, so alterations can be traced.

prompt: Hand-counting sample precincts to check the machines is a random ___.
fact: The random manual audit compares hand counts against machine counts in randomly chosen precincts.

prompt: COMELEC's online tool for locating where you vote is the ___.
fact: Checking the precinct finder before election day avoids being turned away at the wrong polling place.

prompt: The official master record of registered voters is the ___.
fact: The registry is maintained continuously, but registration closes months before an election.

prompt: Voter registration in the Philippines is a ___ process.
fact: Continuing registration runs year-round at local COMELEC offices, pausing only near an election.

prompt: Detainees and some other voters cast their choices using a ___.
fact: Detainee voting lets qualified persons in custody vote without having been convicted by final judgment.

prompt: Officials on duty away from their precinct may use ___ voting.
fact: Local absentee voting covers government workers and media personnel assigned elsewhere on election day.

prompt: Filipinos abroad take part through ___.
fact: Overseas Filipinos register at an embassy or consulate and may vote over a period of about a month.

prompt: The link between voters and those they elect is political ___.
fact: A Kagawad represents the whole barangay, not only the residents who voted for them.

prompt: The formal declaration of a winner is the ___.
fact: Until proclamation there is no winner in law, however clear an unofficial count appears.

prompt: Filling a mid-term vacancy follows the rules of ___.
fact: If a Punong Barangay's post falls vacant, the highest-ranked Kagawad succeeds to the office.

prompt: The duty of officials to answer for their decisions is ___.
fact: Article XI provides for impeachment, removal and criminal liability as the machinery of accountability.

prompt: Making government processes open to inspection is ___.
fact: Barangays must post their budget and projects publicly, so residents can compare spending against plans.

prompt: Taking an active part in public decisions is civic ___.
fact: Voting is periodic; attending the barangay assembly gives residents a say between elections.

prompt: The supreme law of the Philippines is the ___.
fact: The 1987 Constitution created COMELEC as an independent commission so it could not be run by the government of the day.

prompt: Splitting power among branches of government is the ___ of powers.
fact: No single official holds all power, which is why a barangay captain cannot simply overrule a court.

prompt: COMELEC's freedom from political control is its ___.
fact: Its independence is constitutional: COMELEC has its own budget and commissioners with fixed terms.

prompt: Barring someone from office for a legal reason is ___.
fact: Conviction of certain crimes, or committing an election offense, can disqualify a person from holding office.

prompt: Officials must yearly file a statement of assets, liabilities and net worth, known as the ___.
fact: The SALN is a public document, so citizens may inspect whether an official's wealth matches their income.

prompt: A cap on consecutive terms in the same post is a ___.
fact: Under Republic Act 12232 a barangay official may serve at most three consecutive terms in the same post, and an SK official only one.

prompt: One family holding many offices at once is a ___.
fact: The Constitution says the State shall prohibit political dynasties, but Congress has never passed the enabling law.

prompt: Deciding a matter you personally profit from is a ___.
fact: An official should abstain when a barangay contract would benefit their own family or business.

prompt: Decisions serving society rather than private gain serve the ___.
fact: A project chosen because it helps the most residents serves the public interest; one chosen to reward supporters does not.

prompt: Putting a law directly to the voters is a ___.
fact: Referendum, initiative and recall let citizens act directly instead of waiting for the next election.

prompt: Citizens proposing a law themselves use people's ___.
fact: Local initiative lets registered voters propose or repeal a local ordinance by petition.

prompt: Removing a local official by popular vote before the term ends is a ___.
fact: A recall election lets voters replace a local official mid-term, though barangay posts are treated separately.

prompt: Careful public discussion before deciding is ___.
fact: The Sangguniang Barangay must deliberate in session, and its sessions are open to residents.

prompt: Careful management of public resources is ___.
fact: Barangay funds are public money, and their use is audited by the Commission on Audit.

prompt: The principle that officials are bound by law just as citizens are is the ___.
fact: Holding office is not immunity: an official who commits an election offense faces the same law as anyone else.

prompt: Checking whether public actions follow the rules is ___.
fact: The Commission on Audit examines government spending, including at barangay level.

prompt: Campaigning before the official period is ___ campaigning.
fact: Campaign materials may only go up once the COMELEC campaign period has formally begun.

prompt: Replacing a candidate who withdraws or dies is ___.
fact: Substitution is tightly limited by law, and generally requires the substitute to be from the same party.

prompt: Documented past performance in office is a ___.
fact: A record is checkable evidence: completed projects, attendance, and audited spending.

prompt: Weighing what a project gives against what it costs is a ___ analysis.
fact: A covered court and a drainage system may cost the same, so ask which one solves the bigger local problem.

prompt: A completed and verifiable achievement is an ___.
fact: Ask for the completion date and cost; an unfinished project is not an accomplishment.

prompt: Ranking which needs to address first is ___.
fact: Barangay funds are limited, so a credible candidate can explain what they would fund first and why.

prompt: The setting aside of public funds for a purpose is an ___.
fact: The Sangguniang Barangay passes an annual budget ordinance appropriating the barangay's funds.

prompt: The public posting of barangay projects and costs appears on the ___.
fact: Posting projects and their budgets lets any resident check spending without filing a request.

prompt: Asking affected residents before deciding is ___.
fact: Barangay development plans are meant to be drawn up with resident consultation, not written behind closed doors.

prompt: The barangay's programme of projects is its ___.
fact: A project must appear in the barangay development plan before money can properly be spent on it.

prompt: The qualifications a candidate claims are their ___.
fact: Credentials are worth checking: claimed schooling and past positions are matters of public record.

prompt: Giving money or goods in exchange for a vote is ___.
fact: COMELEC's anti-vote-buying drive treats both giver and receiver as liable, and the secret ballot means no buyer can verify the vote.

prompt: False content created deliberately to deceive is ___.
fact: Disinformation is manufactured to mislead; misinformation is the same falsehood passed on in good faith.

prompt: False content shared by someone who believes it is ___.
fact: The remedy is the same for both: trace a claim to its source before passing it on.

prompt: The skill of telling reliable sources from misleading ones is ___.
fact: Check who published a claim, when, and what evidence they showed before believing an election story.

prompt: A formal legal challenge to a result is an ___.
fact: Protests are decided by the courts or COMELEC, not by whoever shouts loudest online.

prompt: A coordinated group paid to push political content online is a ___.
fact: Many accounts posting identical wording at the same time is a sign of coordination rather than public opinion.

prompt: The main government building where many city offices are located is the ___.
fact: City Hall houses the mayor's office, the city council, and the frontline service windows residents use.

prompt: The elected official who serves as the chief executive of a city is the ___.
fact: A city mayor serves a three-year term and may hold no more than three consecutive terms.

prompt: The elected official who can preside over the city council is the ___.
fact: The vice mayor presides over the city council but votes only to break a tie.

prompt: The local legislative body that passes city laws is the ___.
fact: A city's council is the Sangguniang Panlungsod, made up of elected councilors.

prompt: A local law passed by the city council is called an ___.
fact: An ordinance is a local law that carries penalties and stays in force until repealed.

prompt: A formal expression of the city council's decision or position is called a ___.
fact: A resolution expresses the council's position on a matter; it is not a permanent local law.

prompt: An official authorization allowing a person or business to do something is a ___.
fact: Permits let the city check that an activity meets safety, zoning, and health rules before it starts.

prompt: An official document granting legal permission to operate or practice is a ___.
fact: Licenses are issued for a fixed period and must be renewed to stay valid.

prompt: The city official responsible for collecting and managing local revenues is the ___.
fact: The city treasurer collects local taxes and keeps custody of city funds.

prompt: The city official who helps determine property values for taxation is the ___.
fact: The assessor appraises land and buildings so property tax rests on a recorded value.

prompt: The official who keeps and reviews the city's financial records is the ___.
fact: The city accountant keeps the books and certifies that expenses are properly recorded.

prompt: The city official who handles public works and technical construction matters is the ___.
fact: The city engineer reviews building plans and supervises public works projects.

prompt: The office that handles many local public health services is the ___.
fact: The city health office runs immunisation, sanitation, and other frontline health services.

prompt: The office that assists vulnerable families and individuals is the ___.
fact: Social welfare offices assist children, senior citizens, persons with disabilities, and families in crisis.

prompt: The office that records births, marriages, and deaths is the ___.
fact: Civil registry records are the legal proof of a person's birth, marriage, and death.

prompt: A document commonly required before a business can legally operate in the city is a ___.
fact: Business permits are renewed every January, together with the local business tax.

prompt: A document required before many construction projects can legally begin is a ___.
fact: A building permit is issued only after the plans are checked against the National Building Code.

prompt: A document confirming that a completed building may be used is an ___.
fact: The occupancy permit certifies that the finished building is safe to be used.

prompt: A document showing information used to assess real property is a ___.
fact: A tax declaration records a property's assessed value; it is not by itself proof of ownership.

prompt: The tax imposed by the city on land and buildings is called ___.
fact: Real property tax may be paid in full by January or in four quarterly instalments.

prompt: A local tax represented by a community tax certificate is the ___.
fact: The community tax certificate, or cedula, is often required when signing official documents.

prompt: A paper or digital proof that a payment was made is a ___.
fact: Always ask for a receipt: it is the only proof that a payment reached the city's funds.

prompt: A number given to a visitor so they know when it is their turn at a service counter is a ___.
fact: Queue numbers keep service first-come, first-served, so no one can be quietly moved ahead.

prompt: The place where visitors can ask where to go inside City Hall is the ___.
fact: The information desk exists so no resident has to pay a fixer to find the right window.

prompt: Helping residents through government programs and transactions is called ___.
fact: Public office is a public trust: government workers are paid from the taxes residents pay.

prompt: The official emblem used to represent the city government is the ___.
fact: The seal makes a city document official, and forging it is a criminal offence.

prompt: The room where the city council formally meets is the ___.
fact: Council sessions held in the session hall are open to the public.

prompt: The office where the city's chief executive works is the ___.
fact: The mayor's office signs permits, issues executive orders, and heads the city's executive branch.

prompt: The office where local taxes and many city payments are handled is the ___.
fact: Wherever you pay inside City Hall, the transaction should end with a treasury-issued official receipt.

prompt: The office that handles the appraisal and assessment of real property is the ___.
fact: The assessor's office keeps the tax map and the record of every taxable property in the city.

prompt: The office that records and checks financial transactions is the ___.
fact: The accounting office checks that every disbursement carries complete supporting documents.

prompt: The office that handles plans and technical concerns for city infrastructure is the ___.
fact: The engineering office inspects city roads, drainage, and public buildings.

prompt: The office that provides legal advice to the city government is the ___.
fact: The city legal office drafts contracts and defends the city in court.

prompt: The office that helps prepare development plans for the city is the ___.
fact: The planning office prepares the land use plan that guides where the city may grow.

prompt: The office that prepares and monitors the city's proposed expenditures is the ___.
fact: The budget office makes sure no expense is proposed without a source of funds.

prompt: The office that helps manage the city's purchasing and bidding activities is the ___.
fact: Procurement handles bidding so city purchases stay competitive and documented.

prompt: The office where official city documents are filed and stored is the ___.
fact: Records are kept for set retention periods so past decisions can still be checked.

prompt: The employee or window where residents make authorized payments is the ___.
fact: Only an authorized cashier may accept payment, and only against an official receipt.

prompt: The document a person fills out when requesting a service or permit is an ___.
fact: Filling in the form completely the first time is the fastest way through any City Hall transaction.

prompt: A government-issued document commonly used to confirm a person's identity is a ___.
fact: A valid ID protects you: it stops someone else from transacting under your name.

prompt: A person's written name used to approve or certify a document is a ___.
fact: Signing a document means accepting responsibility for what it says.

prompt: The proof of payment issued by an authorized government collecting officer is an ___.
fact: No official receipt, no proof of payment: the simplest defence against collection fraud.

prompt: A person or business that is legally required to pay taxes is a ___.
fact: Local taxes pay for the city's roads, health centres, and scholarships.

prompt: A member of the public who receives local government services is a ___.
fact: Any resident may ask how city funds are spent, because the information is public.

prompt: A document from a barangay that may be requested for some City Hall transactions is a ___.
fact: Barangay clearance shows the barangay has no objection to the transaction.

prompt: A document confirming that a proposed use of land follows zoning rules is a ___.
fact: Zoning clearance confirms the intended use is allowed in that part of the city.

prompt: Compliance intended to protect people from fire hazards is called ___.
fact: The Bureau of Fire Protection inspects a building before a fire safety certificate is issued.

prompt: A permit showing that certain health and sanitation requirements are met is a ___.
fact: Food businesses need a sanitary permit and health cards for their workers.

prompt: The institution that manages public affairs for the entire city is the ___.
fact: A city government has its own council, budget, and taxing powers under the Local Government Code.

prompt: A city is one type of ___ unit in the Philippines.
fact: Provinces, cities, municipalities, and barangays are the four local government units in the Philippines.

prompt: The formal legislative body of a Philippine city is the ___.
fact: The Sangguniang Panlungsod passes the city's ordinances and approves its annual budget.

prompt: The mayor is commonly described as the city's ___.
fact: As local chief executive the mayor enforces laws, signs contracts, and supervises every city office.

prompt: The official who helps coordinate the administrative operations of the city government is the ___.
fact: The city administrator coordinates the day-to-day work of the different city departments.

prompt: The official who keeps the records of city council proceedings is the ___.
fact: The secretary to the Sanggunian keeps the minutes and the official copy of every ordinance.

prompt: The official who gives legal advice and represents the city in legal matters is the ___.
fact: The city legal officer reviews contracts before the mayor signs them.

prompt: The official responsible for preparing and helping administer the city budget is the ___.
fact: The budget officer prepares the annual budget the mayor submits to the council.
